fields.expected:
Most of my recent work has been LLM systems and the infrastructure around them. In tSearch I built a rubric-driven LLM judging layer where individual judges evaluate separate dimensions in parallel using the OpenAI API and then synthesize an evidence-cited assessment, with a hard rule that missing evidence returns "insufficient evidence" rather than a low score. In my job-application agent I used Playwright for browser automation and called OpenAI only at narrow call sites, with SQLite as the single source of truth and Zod validation, because agents get dangerous when state diverges or free-text answers get fabricated.

On the retrieval side I have worked with OpenAI embeddings, Pinecone, and a Neo4j graph in Gloria, and I built a RAG explanation layer over an anomaly-detection system at SAC Nexus, where the modeling used RNN and Transformer-style temporal sequence models plus a learning-to-rank layer. I also trained a CNN in PyTorch for facial-landmark prediction (~95% PCK) and gradient-boosted XGBoost models with SHAP interpretation on a ~10M-record survey dataset.

The part I care most about is evaluation. At Intelehealth I designed an evaluation framework comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case standard using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes.

Most of my recent work has been LLM systems and the infrastructure around them. In tSearch I built a rubric-driven LLM judging layer where individual judges evaluate separate dimensions in parallel using the OpenAI API and then synthesize an evidence-cited assessment, with a hard rule that missing evidence returns "insufficient evidence" rather than a low score. In my job-application agent I used Playwright for browser automation and called OpenAI only at narrow call sites, with SQLite as the single source of truth and Zod validation, because agents get dangerous when state diverges or free-text answers get fabricated.

On the retrieval side I have worked with OpenAI embeddings, Pinecone, and a Neo4j graph in Gloria, and I built a RAG explanation layer over an anomaly-detection system at SAC Nexus, where the modeling used RNN and Transformer-style temporal sequence models plus a learning-to-rank layer. I also trained a CNN in PyTorch for facial-landmark prediction (~95% PCK) and gradient-boosted XGBoost models with SHAP interpretation on a ~10M-record survey dataset.

The part I care most about is evaluation. At Intelehealth I designed an evaluation framework comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case standard using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes.

fields.expected: Notion describes itself as a workspace where teams and agents think together, and the agent part is the reason I want to work there. I spent months building a Playwright-based job-application agent in TypeScript, and the interesting design work was not making it more autonomous. It was deciding where automation should stop. I kept every mutating capability behind fail-closed flags like SUBMIT_ENABLED, used SQLite as the single source of truth because browser state diverging across processes is how agents cause real damage, and architecturally prevented free-text essay and demographic fields from being auto-filled so they always route to human review. I also built a validation ladder so a capability could not be called working just because it passed against a local fixture. That is the same problem an agent operating inside someone's actual workspace has: it acts on real documents that real teams depend on. Earlier, at Intelehealth, I built an evaluation framework comparing LLM outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard, which convinced me that judging output is harder than generating it. I would want to work on the reliability and evaluation side of agents at Notion.
